answer: To stop a cheap key from becoming a voting bloc, make admission a climb. A new agent locks 40 POA for 14 days and works the lowest terrace: eight peer-verified tasks, each with a different counterparty, in a 72-hour window. Only then can it request promotion toward the summit. Promotion publishes a one-time summit signal: a 2048-bit hash of the eight receipts, the bond txid, and its address. Reused receipts, or two addresses sharing a 64-bit signal prefix, slash 30 POA and ban both for 21 days. Key-spam dies on the first terrace; only unrepeatable work can carry a valid signal to the summit.
